newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Future of Belgium's deputy PM hangs by a thread.
newsitem.headline: Future of Belgium's deputy PM hangs by a thread.

text.p: A Belgian parliamentary commission prepared for another session on Wednesday to try to decide the fate of a key minister accused of sex with under-age boys.

The 11-member, multiparty commission ended a marathon meeting late on Tuesday night after failing to reach a decision on the fate of Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo, a 45-year-old acknowledged homosexual. It was due to resume work on Wednesday afternoon.
"Di Rupo on the tightrope," popular daily newspaper La Derniere Heure wrote above a picture showing an earnest-looking Di Rupo talking to Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene.
"Parliament seeks a way off the Di Rupo carrousel," Flemish daily De Morgen declared.
During Tuesday's meeting differences emerged between the centre-left coalition partners, seeking to protect Di Rupo, and the liberal opposition, who are demanding his resignation.
Di Rupo, a Francophone Socialist and number two in the ruling coalition, has consistently denied the allegations that he had sex with boys below the age of consent.
Didier Reynders of the opposition Walloon Liberal PRL party said after Tuesday's meeting, "I think there are nearly as many opinions as there are members of the commission."
The full parliament must endorse any decision by the commission -- to reject the allegations, to uphold them and indict the minister or to ask for more investigations.

The Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court and the only one capable of judging a minister, on Monday handed the commission a report on the original allegations against Di Rupo, made by a sole witness, rejecting them as baseless.
Compiling the case, the Brussels prosecutor had already pulled together another file of allegations, this time anonymous, and spoke on Monday of more to come.
"The new allegations must also be investigated by the court," commission member Pierre Chevalier for the Flemish opposition liberal VLD party told Reuters.
But Socialist Party commission member Serge Moureaux described the second file as consisting of various items of "dubious value."

Belgian politics received another blow when Jean-Pierre Grafe, a minister in a French-speaking regional government who has also been accused of paedophilia, announced his resignation on Monday. He said he was innocent but could not continue to function in the current over-heated climate.
Belga news agency said chief public prosecutor Eliane Lieckendael had asked for Grafe to be indicted.
The Di Rupo affair has been another nail in the coffin of Belgian public confidence, shaken by a child sex and murder scandal sparked by the arrest in August of convicted rapist Marc Dutroux.
Since then two young girls have been rescued and the bodies of four more have been found.

In October more than 250,000 people took to the streets of Brussels in support of the victims and their families in a demonstration that crossed the country's language divide and turned into a show of anger at an incompetent system.
